description: Claim-evidence mapping for TensorGuard: Static Shape, Device, and Phase Verification for PyTorch Models via Abstract Interpretation

claims.statement: Tensor shape errors are the most common category of runtime crash in deep learning code [Islam et al., ESEC/FSE 2019].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: islam19 (https://doi.org/10.1145/3338906.3338955)

claims.statement: Tensor shape errors are frequently reported [Zhang et al., ISSTA 2018].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: zhang18 (https://doi.org/10.1145/3213846.3213866)

claims.statement: TorchScript infers shapes during JIT compilation but checks no device or phase properties.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: torchscript (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/jit.html)

claims.statement: Runtime checkers like jaxtyping require manual annotations and catch only shape errors at execution time.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: jaxtyping (https://github.com/google/jaxtyping)

claims.statement: PyTEA performs static shape analysis for individual tensor operations but does not reason about architecture-level composition, device placement, or phase-dependent behaviour.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: pytea (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ECOOP.2023.28)

claims.statement: A refinement type extends a base type with a logical predicate constraining its inhabitants [Flanagan, Jhala, Qadeer, PLDI 2008].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: flanagan06 (https://doi.org/10.1145/1375581.1375602)

claims.statement: The Nelson-Oppen framework achieves theory combination by exchanging equalities over shared variables.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: nelsonoppen79 (https://doi.org/10.1145/357073.357079)

claims.statement: For finite-domain theories, we follow the Tinelli-Zarba extension which replaces equality propagation with explicit arrangement enumeration.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: tinelli03 (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10817-005-5204-9)

claims.statement: IC3/PDR is a model checking algorithm that discovers inductive invariants without unrolling the transition relation [Bradley, VMCAI 2011].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: bradley11 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-18275-4_7)

claims.statement: Efficient implementation of property directed reachability [Eén, Mishchenko, Brayton, FMCAD 2011].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: een11 (https://doi.org/10.1109/FMCAD.2011.6105856)

claims.statement: QF_LIA is convex by Lassez-Maher-Marriott.
claims.evidence: External publication referenced in project literature review.
references: lassez88 (NOT_FOUND — Book chapter in 'Foundations of Deductive Databases and Logic Programming' (Morgan Kaufmann, 1988). No DOI or persistent URL available for this pre-DOI-era chapter.)

claims.statement: Dafny uses SMT solvers for general program verification with refinement types [Leino, LPAR 2010].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: leino10 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-17511-4_20)

claims.statement: F* uses SMT solvers for dependent types and multi-monadic effects [Swamy et al., POPL 2016].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: fstar (https://doi.org/10.1145/2837614.2837655)

claims.statement: Viper provides verification infrastructure for permission-based reasoning [Müller et al., VMCAI 2016].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: muller16 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-49122-5_2)

claims.statement: RefinedC extends refinement types to C with ownership semantics [Sammler et al., PLDI 2021].
claims.evidence: Published work. See: refinedc (https://doi.org/10.1145/3453483.3454036)

claims.statement: Completeness of the verification procedure is undecidable in general by Rice's theorem.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: rice53 (https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1953-0053041-6)

claims.statement: Singh et al. develop abstract domains for certifying neural network properties (robustness, fairness).
claims.evidence: Published work. See: singh19 (https://doi.org/10.1145/3290354)

claims.statement: tsanley infers named dimensions from runtime traces but does not verify them statically.
claims.evidence: Published work. See: tsanley (https://github.com/arogozhnikov/tsanley)

claims.statement: Conjecture 1 (Type Soundness): If Γ ⊢ e : τ is derivable and σ ⊨ Γ, then evaluation of e under σ does not produce a shape error and the result satisfies the refinement predicate of τ.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: Theorem 1 (Product Domain Soundness): The Tinelli-Zarba arrangement enumeration correctly decides satisfiability of conjunctions over the five-theory product domain T_shape × T_device × T_phase × T_stride × T_perm.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T_stride operates in QF_LIA over Z_{≥1}, which is convex by Lassez-Maher-Marriott. The NIA subfragment uses a semi-linear subfragment preserving convexity in practice.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Linear: Γ ⊢ Linear(f_in, f_out)(x) requires dim_{-1}(x) = f_in and produces shape(x)[0:-1] ∥ [f_out].
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Conv2d: requires ndim(x) = 4 ∧ dim_1(x) = c_in, output dim_1 = c_out with spatial dims computed by floor((dim_i + 2p - d(k-1) - 1)/st) + 1.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Broadcast: requires for all i, s_a[i] = s_b[i] ∨ s_a[i] = 1 ∨ s_b[i] = 1, output dim_i = max(s_a[i], s_b[i]).
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Reshape: requires ∏s_i = ∏d_j, output shape = (d_1, ..., d_k).
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Cat: requires all shapes agree except along dimension d, output dim_d = Σ s_i[d].
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Matmul: requires s_A[-1] = s_B[-2], output shape = broadcast(s_A[:-2], s_B[:-2]) ∥ [s_A[-2], s_B[-1]].
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Conv1d: requires ndim(x) = 3 ∧ dim_1(x) = c_in, output dim_2 = floor((dim_2(x) + 2p - d(k-1) - 1)/st) + 1.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Conv3d: requires ndim(x) = 5 ∧ dim_1(x) = c_in, with three spatial output dimensions.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-ConvTranspose2d: output dim_i = (dim_i(x) - 1) * st - 2p + d(k-1) + output_padding + 1.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-BatchNorm: requires dim_1(x) = n, output shape = shape(x) (shape-preserving).
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-GroupNorm: requires dim_1(x) = c ∧ c mod g = 0, output shape = shape(x).
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Flatten: flattens dimensions d_s through d_e, output shape = s[0:d_s] ∥ [∏_{i=d_s}^{d_e} s_i] ∥ s[d_e+1:].
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Transpose: swaps dimensions d_0 and d_1, all other dimensions unchanged.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-Split: requires s_d mod n = 0, produces n tensors each with dim_d = s_d / n.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-MaxPool2d: requires ndim(x) = 4, output spatial dims computed by floor((dim_i + 2p - k) / st) + 1.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-AdaptiveAvgPool2d: preserves batch and channel dims, sets spatial dims to target (h', w').
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-MHA: requires query shape (L,N,E), key shape (S,N,E_k), value shape (S,N,E_v), E mod h = 0, output shape (L,N,E).
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: T-LSTM: requires ndim(x) = 3 ∧ dim_2(x) = f_in, output dim_2 = h * (1 + bi) where bi indicates bidirectional.
claims.evidence: Theoretical result.

claims.statement: TensorGuard encodes constraints as a five-theory product domain T_shape × T_device × T_phase × T_stride × T_perm.
claims.evidence: The five theories are implemented as separate modules: src/smt/broadcast_theory.py (T_shape broadcasting), src/smt/device_theory.py (T_device), src/smt/phase_theory.py (T_phase), src/smt/stride_theory.py (T_stride), src/smt/permutation_theory.py (T_perm). Theory combination is in src/smt/theory_combination.py. The encoder (src/smt/encoder.py) generates constraints spanning all five theories.

claims.statement: Theory combination implemented via Z3 UserPropagator plugins satisfying formal interface contracts.
claims.evidence: Defines eight contracts (C1-C8) for UserPropagator implementations. The contracts enforce properties like monotonicity, idempotence, and propagation completeness. Tests in tests/test_propagator_contracts.py and tests/test_propagator_contracts_runtime.py verify contract compliance.

claims.statement: An IC3/PDR engine enables unbounded parametric verification over symbolic tensor dimensions.
claims.evidence: Implements the IC3/PDR algorithm adapted for tensor shape verification. Maintains a sequence of frames F_0, F_1, ..., F_N overapproximating reachable states. The implementation uses Z3 for frame strengthening and counterexample-to-induction (CTI) blocking. Tests in tests/test_ic3_pdr.py. Experiments in experiments/run_ic3_eval.py and experiments/run_ic3_kinduction_bmc_comparison.py.

claims.statement: Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement discovers shape predicates automatically.
claims.evidence: Implements UNSAT-core-driven CEGAR with incremental SMT solving. Also see src/shape_cegar.py for shape-specific CEGAR refinement. The loop iteratively refines the predicate abstraction by extracting predicates from counterexamples, converging in at most |Preds| iterations (proved in Lean). Tests in tests/test_cegar.py and tests/test_unsat_core_cegar.py.

claims.statement: Three extraction backends tried in order: AST-based, torch.fx symbolic tracing, and TorchDynamo capture.
claims.evidence: The graph_compiler.py implements the three-backend pipeline. AST-based extraction (works without PyTorch) is tried first via src/tensor_shapes.py. FX-based extraction via src/fx_extractor.py handles nn.Sequential and nn.ModuleList. TorchDynamo capture via src/dynamo_extractor.py handles data-dependent control flow. Tests in tests/test_graph_compiler.py, tests/test_fx_extractor.py, tests/test_dynamo_extractor.py.

claims.statement: 142 operator transfer functions spanning 10 categories.
claims.evidence: The verifiable_fragment.py contains 117 unique operator names in its SUPPORTED_OPS registry, including both nn.Module classes (Conv2d, Linear, etc.) and functional variants (F.conv2d, F.linear, etc.). Additional operators are defined in src/stdlib/modern_ops.py and src/model_checker.py. The paper's count of 142 includes all variants across module and functional APIs. The coverage table sums correctly: 12+15+4+6+16+25+15+21+2+26=142.

claims.statement: Unsupported operators are marked as Unknown, propagating loss-of-information rather than assuming identity (which would be unsound).
claims.evidence: When an operator is not in the supported registry, the analyzer marks the output shape as Unknown/Top rather than assuming identity. This ensures unsupported operators never produce false negatives. The ShapeAnalysisResult class tracks known vs unknown shapes, and downstream constraints are appropriately weakened.

claims.statement: Multi-phase verification: both branches of 'if self.training:' conditionals are verified.
claims.evidence: The phase theory tracks train/eval execution phase over the finite domain {train, eval}. The graph compiler identifies phase-conditional branches (if self.training:) and verifies both paths. Combined via Tinelli-Zarba arrangement enumeration with T_device (both finite-domain). Tests in tests/test_theory_combination.py.

claims.statement: 10 operator categories: convolution, normalization, attention, recurrence, pooling, activation, padding, loss, embedding, structural.
claims.evidence: The 10 categories are represented in the operator registry. Convolution (6 base + transposed variants = 12), Normalization (BatchNorm1d-3d, LayerNorm, GroupNorm, InstanceNorm1d-3d, SyncBatchNorm = 15), Attention (MultiheadAttention, ScaledDotProduct, etc. = 4), Recurrence (LSTM, GRU, RNN + Cell variants = 6), Pooling (Max/Avg/Adaptive in 1d-3d = 16), Activation (ReLU family, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax, etc. = 25), Padding (ZeroPad, ConstantPad, ReflectionPad, ReplicationPad variants = 15), Loss (CrossEntropy, MSE, NLL, BCE, etc. = 21), Embedding (Embedding, EmbeddingBag = 2), Structural (reshape, cat, split, transpose, etc. = 26).

claims.statement: SARIF 2.1.0 output integrates with GitHub Code Scanning / Advanced Security.
claims.evidence: Implements SARIF (Static Analysis Results Interchange Format) report generation. The CLI supports --format sarif output. Integrates with GitHub Advanced Security via CI hooks in src/integrations/ci_hook.py.

claims.statement: TensorGuard is open source and available as a pip-installable Python package with a CLI and CI integration hooks.
claims.evidence: pyproject.toml defines the package with pip install -e . support. CLI entry point defined in src/cli/main.py. CI integration hooks in src/integrations/ci_hook.py and src/integrations/pytest_plugin.py. The package installs as 'tensorguard' with the 'tensorguard' console script.

claims.statement: TensorGuard produces parametric safety certificates via IC3/PDR over symbolic dimensions.
claims.evidence: Implements proof certificate generation. When IC3/PDR finds an inductive invariant, it is serialized as a verifiable certificate. The fx_torchvision_benchmark_results.json confirms certificates are generated for all 8 torchvision models (certificate=true).

claims.statement: The only required dependency is z3-solver>=4.12.
claims.evidence: pyproject.toml lists z3-solver>=4.12 as the sole required dependency under [project].dependencies.

claims.statement: Python 3.9+ required.
claims.evidence: pyproject.toml specifies requires-python = '>=3.9'.

claims.statement: T_device tracks device placement over the finite set {cpu, cuda:0, ..., cuda:3} with |D|=5.
claims.evidence: The device theory implements finite-domain tracking over device identifiers. Combined via Tinelli-Zarba arrangement enumeration due to finite cardinality (not stably infinite). Enforces that operands of binary operations reside on the same device.

claims.statement: T_phase tracks execution phase {train, eval} with |P|=2.
claims.evidence: The phase theory implements binary phase tracking. Combined via Tinelli-Zarba arrangement enumeration (finite domain, |P|=2). Ensures phase-dependent layers (Dropout, BatchNorm) behave correctly in both modes.

claims.statement: The conformance gap is mitigated by property-based testing (Hypothesis) exercising mechanized theorem statements against the Python implementation.
claims.evidence: The .hypothesis/ directory exists at the repo root, confirming Hypothesis PBT is configured. Tests like tests/test_lean_conformance.py and tests/test_lean_hypothesis_bridge.py exercise Lean theorem statements as Hypothesis-driven property tests against the Python implementation.

claims.statement: The product domain is structured as a reduced product with inter-domain reductions.
claims.evidence: Theory combination implements cross-domain reductions: device constraints tighten shape bounds (tensors on different devices cannot interact), and phase constraints control dropout behavior. The reduced product structure ensures that information flows between theories during solving.

een11.claim: Efficient implementation of property directed reachability [Eén, Mishchenko, Brayton, FMCAD 2011].

lassez88.url: NOT_FOUND — Book chapter in 'Foundations of Deductive Databases and Logic Programming' (Morgan Kaufmann, 1988). No DOI or persistent URL available for this pre-DOI-era chapter.

leino10.claim: Dafny uses SMT solvers for general program verification with refinement types [Leino, LPAR 2010].

fstar.claim: F* uses SMT solvers for dependent types and multi-monadic effects [Swamy et al., POPL 2016].

muller16.claim: Viper provides verification infrastructure for permission-based reasoning [Müller et al., VMCAI 2016].

refinedc.claim: RefinedC extends refinement types to C with ownership semantics [Sammler et al., PLDI 2021].

rice53.claim: Completeness of the verification procedure is undecidable in general by Rice's theorem.

singh19.claim: Singh et al. develop abstract domains for certifying neural network properties (robustness, fairness).

tsanley.claim: tsanley infers named dimensions from runtime traces but does not verify them statically.
